name: Best Hardware (2026 name)
also_known_as: Best Hardware in 2023, 2024 and 2025 as well; the name did not change. The 2026 ballot adds a user-testing question that the earlier ballots did not ask.
ballot: Does the hardware you developed address a need or problem in synthetic biology?
Did the team conduct user testing and learn from user feedback?
Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?
Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

winners.note: Four nominees (BIT-China, Estonia-TUBI, NUDT-CHINA, Rochester); no tie. The page is titled 'Adaptive Reaction Chamber' and carries its own 'Best Undergraduate Hardware 2025' banner. Its operating manual is an embedded PDF (general-operating-manual.pdf); the module CAD files are called open-sourced in the text but are not linked from the page.

Two nominees (Brno Czech Republic, ETH-Zurich); no tie. Two devices on one page, a random positioning machine and a DIY bioreactor. The prototype's DBTL iterations are cross-referenced to https://2025.igem.wiki/tudarmstadt/engineering#rpm, and the build files are GitLab raw downloads (3D_print_RPM.zip, RPM_microgravity.gcode) plus two embedded PDFs.

Four nominees (Cambridge, HiZJU-China, Kyoto, NU-Kazakhstan); no tie. /hardware is a 445-word hub. The prize-winning documentation is on /hardware/bioreactor/ (5,156 words, three Design History File PDFs) and /hardware/microfluidic-pump/ (323 words). Neither subpage is reachable from the site: the hub's three project cards are images with no href and the nav lists only top-level pages, and both URLs resolve only with a trailing slash (302 without). The third project, Multiphase Microfluidic Chips, has a card but no published page; five candidate slugs return 404.

One nominee (EPFL); no tie. Device is MAIK, a colorimeter, plus a microfluidic chip. Build instructions, CAD and code sit behind two accordion folds that link three static.igem.wiki PDFs and two GitLab folders; the hardware DBTL iterations are deferred to https://2024.igem.wiki/aachen/engineering.

One nominee (WrightState-OH); no tie. Three devices on one continuous page with a table of contents: a 96-well plate illuminator, a lux sensor and a digital microfluidics platform. The page says the CAD and PCB files are documented but links no file; the only repository link is the generic footer GitLab link.

unawarded.note: No undergraduate winner. The 2023 results page lists the Best Hardware undergraduate Winner slot empty, with four nominees beneath it (HUST-China, Kyoto, OUC-China, Rochester), while the overgraduate and high school slots are filled. Confirmed twice: in the shared render at .render/results-2023.html and in an independent re-render of https://competition.igem.org/results/2023?tab=special-prizes on 2026-10-12. This is not a combined-section year: the two collegiate sections were awarded separately, so the undergraduate award appears to have gone unawarded rather than merged. No team name is recorded here because none is published.
